headline: Adaptive and physics-informed models forecast COVID-19 and glucose trajectories
label: Health Time Series Forecasting
summary: Recent preprints benchmark adaptive ensembles, physics-informed regularization, and multimodal CGM data for epidemic and diabetes forecasting.
synthesis: Across these preprints, the common thread is forecasting health time series by augmenting purely data-driven predictors with external structure: adaptive model weighting, mechanistic constraints, or multimodal covariates. The COVID-19 study applies multi-armed bandit strategies (UCB, EXP3, epsilon-greedy) to weight ensemble members over time, with EXP3 variants reported to perform best on average. The physics-informed study regularizes machine learning forecasts of cases, hospitalizations and the reproduction number with SIHR differential equations, linking epidemiological dynamics to predictive fitting. MetaboNet-Bench contributes an open-source multimodal benchmark for type 1 diabetes glucose forecasting that combines CGM, insulin and carbohydrate inputs and evaluates several models. The novelty lies in sequential decision-making for ensemble combination, mechanistic regularization of epidemic forecasts, and shared benchmarking infrastructure for metabolic time series.
